block.text: #209 folded in: the tools are named by what they do; a block's values are a sentence in the form, defaulted from the pairing picked in Meets, beside the Meets list that motivates them; the block ghosts the tags it would write under the pointer before the click. The side column never changes meaning with the tool.

placing.text: The owner's direction (2026-09-19): a transition is SPELLED — its values as pickers — and PLACED with one button; then a value is swapped and the next one placed. The board below walks the five steps. 'And a third' is gone; the third value is a slot like the others, and filling it makes the block 6 × 6.

premise.text: PROPOSED, not decided. The owner's premise: Materials and Terrain sets are two dressings of the same list — the tagger's palette is the project's materials, and the Materials page's coverage is a query over the tags the tagger writes. One section, the material as its subject, three views of it.

questions.text: OPEN: (1) drawn to the 2026-09-18 ruling that a material spans archetypes — the Archetype select is gone and Face is a switch; wait for the model, or ship the select as interim? (2) three views, or 3D replacing Preview for walls and ramps? (3) tagging controls in the form column. (4) Erase as a tool, not a list row. (5) coverage as a number or a 15-cell bar.

side.text: The side column is the materials list and only that, one flat list by priority with face icons. The selected material expands: its pairings as a vertical list (on its own, meets X…), the lit one the subject of every view, and New transition… below them (the owner's direction, 2026-09-19). Slots (Fringe, Picket, seams) are chips in the Tagging block. Coverage is project-wide. Nothing leaves the list: right-click, or the Erase tool.

threed.text: 3D is the runtime's own RuntimeScene on a generated fixture, with the real atlas, flaps, pickets and fallback, and Show missing on — so a hole reads as the magenta mark it would be on the map. Drawn here as a stand-in. Default view: Preview for floors, 3D for anything with a wall or ramp in it.

round2.text: Round two: the archetype is the context, the slot is picked on the stage — decided 2026-09-19, details open

context.text: DECIDED 2026-09-19. The switch in the bar is the CONTEXT — which archetype we are working with, for every view — and the dropdown on the stage picks the SLOTS that archetype has. One control for what you see and what you write; the Show filter and the Slot and For fields go. A small preview floats on the Tag stage, 2D or 3D, so the result is visible while tagging.

discuss.text: DECIDED: a ramp's surface is 1 × 1½ and keeps the surface's corner tags; a rail is the ramp's trim with a style per material, sheared or upright; stairs are ramp art for now (tentative). STILL OPEN, on the board to the left: two runs or four; long cells on a square sheet or sheets of their own; whether strips keep corner tags; whether Head, Foot and Side are real slots.

rails.text: PROPOSED 2026-09-19, for the owner's call. A rail is tagged like a fringe: three tiles told apart by which of the two TOP corners carry the rail slot — start cap, middle, end cap. The mesher walks the ramp's open side in half-tile pieces and picks each piece's tile by whether the rail carries on past it. Sheared: three pieces per cell along the slope. Upright: two pieces per cell, each stepping down half a tile. Caps at head and foot in both.
